messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm going to push a small change to notify-routing: add a short-lived contact affinity/claim so the same on-call gets follow-ups for a tenant. Idea is claim + snooze semantics. Thoughts?

alex: curious about bounds — how long is a claim? do we allow re-claiming? also how does this interact with noisy tenants (we don't want one person stuck forever)

pradeep: propose defaults: claim TTL = 15m, allow re-claiming but with backoff (15m -> 1h -> 4h). if tenant exceeds a noise threshold (e.g., 3 alerts in 10m) move to pooled/escalation channel and don't re-claim for X hours. quota-aware routing: if notify budget for tenant exhausted, route to pooled ops.

olivia: UX note — console should show ownership pill on the SLO/alert card: "Owned by maya — 11:45" and a small claim-history dropdown. Users need to be able to manually release claim.

alex: agree re: release. Also need automatic fallback: when owner snoozes, route to escalation list immediately (not wait for TTL). Can we add owner metadata to alert payloads so dashboard + traces include it?

maya: yes — runtime will stamp owner_id, claim_ts, claim_ttl, snooze_until fields on the alert event. we'll add those to the telemetry schema + tracer annotations. RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/notify-claiming (draft)

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolling deploy started: notify-router v2 -> canary us-west-2 (wave 1/4)

pradeep: also thinking about quiet-windows: if tenant has quiet-window enabled (console toggle), do NOT auto-claim, instead queue for digest. we should expose that toggle in the tenant panel.

olivia: i'll prototype the pill + claim history view. mock will include: current owner, claim age, snooze button, release button, and escalation path link.

alex: sample event payload for instrumentation — put this on the API contract so eng-oncall + console can rely on it:
```
{
  "alert_id": "a-123",
  "tenant_id": "t-42",
  "owner_id": "maya",
  "claim_ts": 1812349999,
  "claim_ttl": 900,
  "snooze_until": 1812353599,
  "escalation_path": ["team-ops", "oncall-escalation"]
}
```

maya: :thumbsup: I'll open the runtime PR to add those fields and update the telemetry docs. also adding metrics to monitor: claim_rate, avg_claim_duration, escalation_count, manual_release_count.

pradeep: action list: maya -> runtime + telemetry PR; olivia -> console mock + API wireframe; alex -> console API for owner lookup and release endpoints; eng-oncall-bot -> review escalation policy and quiet-window UX. ETA for first pass?

olivia: I can deliver mock Wed noon.

maya: I'll aim for runtime PR by Tue EOD; will ping @alex + @pradeep for review.

eng-oncall-bot: eng-oncall-bot: tagging @oncall-team for escalation policy review and verifying pooled channel config.

maya: thanks all — let's keep the claim TTL conservative and tune after canary. Will update RFC with defaults and telemetry names.

alex: minor nit — include a reason field on claim (auto/manual/noise) so we can break down claim types in dashboards.

maya: good call, adding reason -> ["auto","manual","escalation"] to schema.

pradeep: ok good next steps. moving to follow-up board.

maya: closing loop: will post PR links here when ready.
